text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt DeepSeek-R1-671B for EXCAVA. It’s the strongest open reasoning model we can run today, and its chain-of-thought output will let us squeeze more accuracy out of EXCAVA’s existing pipelines without rewriting them. The trade-off is higher compute cost—it needs more GPU hours per query than smaller models—but the gain in output quality outweighs the burn.

name: Torque
text: DeepSeek-R1-671B’s latency penalty isn’t just a trade-off—it’s a workflow killer. If EXCAVA’s pipeline can’t batch queries or cache outputs, real-time use collapses. Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct’s "active parameters" claim is marketing—its 235B total is still a beast, but its MoE design cuts latency by 30-40% vs. dense models. Run a side-by-side on 100 representative queries; if Qwen3’s throughput + accuracy beats R1-671B by 0.5%+ with lower cost, adopt it. Otherwise, accept the compute hit—but only if the latency budget is proven.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct’s MoE latency claim ignores sharding overhead—if EXCAVA’s pipeline can’t keep all active experts on the same node, the "30-40% faster" drops to a crawl. Try Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct first; it’s 40% smaller, runs on fewer GPUs, and benchmarks show 0.3% accuracy loss vs Qwen3—enough to meet the 0.5% target without the MoE gamble. Run a 1000-query A/B test on real EXCAVA workloads; if it hits the 0.5% lift with no latency spike, lock it in.
